criteria.h1: The measurement chart of a child's body, kept with the costume order
tableRows: Easy AppointmentsDocumented self-hosted appointment plugin marketed for service businesses (plugin version 4.0.3). WordPress admin screens cover locations, services, workers, an appointments list, a customer list, custom form fields, and CSV export. A Saturday trial class or a private-lesson slot is a booking you create; a service name such as trial class or private lesson is a label you configure. Neither is a documented default. Child-name-and-age, class-level, costume-measurements, medical-conditions, photo-release, or emergency-contact questions are custom fields you add (textarea, select, input, or checkbox); they are not documented defaults. A booking is a calendar row, not an enrollment — and a CSV export of a trial-class row next to a child name and a measurement note is still a calendar that holds a body chart beside a contact name. Emails can include those custom fields and copy the appointment off-site. An optional GDPR setting can auto-remove customer data older than six months; that is not a default purge. Google Calendar, SMS, and payments are Pro. Google reCAPTCHA is optional. Public booking-form browser hosts are unverified. | Trial-class and private-lesson bookings stored on your WordPress site | Browser hosts not verified | Not assessed | Not tested | None | WordPress.org listingv4.0.3 readme.txt (SVN)

The listing states Forminator stores and organizes submissions so you can sort, analyze, and manage responses, and includes a free file-upload field with multi-file support. Version 1.58.1 helper-fields.php forminator_upload_root() writes under the WordPress uploads directory plus /forminator/, with per-form hashed subfolders from forminator_get_upload_path(). upload.php stores files through that path. Child-name-and-age, class-level, costume-measurements, medical-conditions, photo-release, or emergency-contact fields are fields you add; they are not documented defaults. Completing the form can store bust, waist, hips, and girth next to a child name and age, a class level, a medical-conditions note, a photo-release checkbox, an emergency contact, and optional recital-headshot uploads — typed once as the measurement chart of a child's body, kept with the costume order, into the same tables as a newsletter signup. A measurement set is what a parent taped and typed, not a fitting record. A medical-conditions answer is the parent's note, not a chart. A photo-release checkbox is a stored preference, not a mechanism that deletes or retrieves anything — and a staff login can open "Maya, age 8, Level 2, bust 24 waist 22 hips 26 girth 38, asthma stage left, photo release yes, dad cell, recital headshot.jpg" next to everyone else's resume. A child named in the form never touched it. Notification emails can copy field values and files off-site. Optional Stripe, PayPal, HubSpot, Mailchimp, and webhook integrations send data only when you enable them.
